translation.text:
After I had prayed in the house and sat down on the couch[a], a certain man entered, glorious in appearance, in shepherd’s attire, wearing a white skin, and having a bag on his shoulders and a staff in his hand. And he greeted me, and I returned his greeting.

2. And immediately he sat beside me and says to me, “I have been sent by the most venerable angel, that I may dwell with you for the rest of the days of your life.”

3. I thought that he had come to test me, and I say to him, “Who then are you? For I,” I say, “know the one to whom I was handed over.” He says to me, “Do you not recognize me?” “No,” I say. “I,” he says, “am the Shepherd to whom you were entrusted.”

4. While he was still speaking, his appearance was changed, and I recognized him, that he was the one to whom I had been entrusted, and immediately I was confounded, and fear seized me, and I was completely crushed with grief, because I had answered him so wickedly and senselessly.

5. But he answered me and says, “Do not be confounded, but be strengthened in my mandates, which I am about to command you. For I have been sent,” he says, “that I may show you again all the things you saw before, especially the main points that are beneficial for you. First of all, write my mandates and the parables; but the other things, as I show you, so you will write.” For this reason, he says, “I command you first to write the mandates and parables, so that you may read them readily at hand and be able to keep them.”

6. So I wrote the mandates and the parables, just as he commanded me.

7. If then, having heard them, you keep them and walk in them and do them with a pure heart, you will receive from the Lord what he promised you; but if, having heard, you do not repent[h], but still add to your sins, you will receive from the Lord the opposite things. The Shepherd, the angel of repentance[g][f][e][d][c][b], commanded me to write all these things in this way.

footnotes.text: Shepherd’s attire: white skin, bag, and staff were typical of pastoral imagery, signaling the figure’s role and purity in the vision.
The verb ἀσπάζομαι means “to greet”; in early Christian contexts, greetings could include a kiss (cf. Rom 16:16), but the text here simply says “greeted.”
“Mandates” translates ἐντολαί; many English versions read “commandments,” but Hermas uses ἐντολαί as a section title for his paraenetic instructions.
“Parables” renders παραβολαί and corresponds to the section often called the “Similitudes.”
“Main points” translates κεφάλαια, which can mean principal matters or summaries; it does not here denote book chapters.
The pronoun “you” in “beneficial for you” is plural (ὑμῖν), indicating that the instruction is for the community, not only Hermas.
“Testing me” translates ἐκπειράζων με; the nuance is of examination or proving, not enticing to sin.

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

lexical_decisions.rationale: σχῆμα denotes outward form/appearance; paired with ποιμενικός, it conveys attire/appearance of a shepherd. "Guise" keeps visual register.
δέρμα is an animal skin/hide; context suggests garment of skin. Retaining "skin" preserves the concrete image.

lexical_decisions.chosen: with a bag on his shoulders
alternatives: with a wallet on his shoulders
with a scrip over his shoulders
lexical_decisions.rationale: πήρα is a leather pouch/scrip (esp. of travelers/shepherds). "Bag" is accessible modern English; 'scrip' is archaic.
ῥάβδος can be rod/staff. Given shepherd imagery, "staff" fits best.
ἀσπάζομαι commonly means to greet/salute; physical embrace is not explicit here.
παρα-καθίζω conveys sitting down near/beside someone. "Beside" captures proximity.
σεμνός denotes dignity/augustness. "Venerable" communicates solemn dignity without conflating with "holy" (ἅγιος).
οἰκέω often denotes dwelling/settled presence; "dwell" preserves theological resonance of ongoing presence.
ἐκπειράζω means to test thoroughly; "testing" avoids the moral connotation of enticing to sin that "tempting" can carry.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to whom I was handed over
lexical_decisions.rationale: παραδίδωμι here has the sense of being committed/handed over to someone’s charge; "handed over" preserves the formal tone and echoes Hermas's own phrasing.
ἰδέα is outward appearance/form. "Appearance was changed" is clear and literal.
συγχέω in passive indicates confusion/embarrassment. "Confounded" retains elevated tone.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I was completely broken down with grief
alternatives: I was utterly crushed with grief
I was cut down by grief
lexical_decisions.rationale: συνκόπτω metaphorically of being shattered; "broken down" plus "with grief" conveys intensity; "completely" renders ὅλος.
πονηρός = wicked/evil; ἄφρων = senseless/foolish. Pairing retains moral and cognitive nuance.

alternatives: be made strong by my commandments
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἰσχυροποιέω = make strong; middle imperative urges being strengthened. ἐντολή is rendered "mandate" here to reflect Hermas’s internal section title and maintain consistency across the work.
κεφάλαιον can denote a principal point or summary. "Main points" fits the explanatory sense without implying book chapters.
σύμφορος means beneficial/advantageous. "Beneficial" is clear and idiomatic.

lexical_decisions.chosen: have them at hand to read
alternatives: keep them at the ready to read
lexical_decisions.rationale: Idiomatic expression for ready availability; "at hand" preserves the idiom transparently.
φυλάσσω in moral instruction often = keep/observe commandments. "Keep" is concise and standard.
πορεύομαι with ἐν conveys conduct of life. "Walk in" retains biblical ethical metaphor common in early Christian texts.
ἐργάζομαι of doing/working deeds; "put into practice" connects hearing to doing, matching paraenetic tone.

alternatives: you will receive ... what is contrary
you will receive ... the contrary things
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐναντίος = opposite/contrary. Rendering preserves antithetical structure.

lexical_decisions.source_word: ὁ ποιμήν ... ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς μετανοίας
alternatives: the shepherd, the angel of repentance

theological_decisions.rationale: σεμνός emphasizes dignified, august character rather than moral purity per se; "venerable" captures reverential dignity.
To avoid suggesting the figure entices to sin; the context is an evaluative test of recognition.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Capitalize "Shepherd" when referring to the visionary figure identified as ὁ ποιμήν.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Keep English "you" (ambiguous number) but annotate that the Greek shifts to plural, indicating community-wide instruction.

theological_decisions.rationale: English lacks a standard plural "you"; footnote marks the communal scope without altering the register.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Transparency principle: preserve ambiguity and annotate.

theological_decisions.rationale: Greek uses παραβολαί; translating as "parables" follows the source while still guiding readers to the book’s structure via note.

review_passes.summary: The draft is exceptionally accurate and captures the register and vocabulary of Hermas perfectly. I made one minor adjustment in verse 3 to translate the inferential γὰρ ('Who, then, are you?').
issues_found: In verse 3, the Greek reads 'Σὺ γὰρ τίς εἶ;' The draft omits the inferential γὰρ. Adding 'then' ('Who, then, are you?') captures the logical connection to Hermas's suspicion that he is being tested.
